note: Research categories a country lead may assign to scouts. Choose by what the window needs; none is mandatory. Third-country developments that bear on US-China competition belong to the category they affect.

categories.title: Policy and regulation
categories.scope: Laws, rules, industrial policy, AI governance and procurement rules that affect AI or chips; legislative bills with a realistic path.

categories.title: Export controls and sanctions
categories.scope: Export and import controls, licences, entity and sanctions lists, enforcement cases and countermeasures, including rules that bind third-country firms (Netherlands, Japan, Malaysia, Taiwan).

categories.title: AI models and capabilities
categories.scope: Frontier and open-weight model releases, capability or efficiency shifts, training on domestic hardware, evaluations with a competitive bearing.

categories.title: Semiconductor companies and supply chains
categories.scope: Foundry, memory, equipment, materials and packaging; capacity, yields, substitution milestones; TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix, ASML and peers where they affect US-China competition.

categories.title: Computing infrastructure
categories.scope: Data centres, accelerator supply and allocation, cloud access, chip diversion and smuggling routes, power constraints.

categories.title: Significant corporate and market developments
categories.scope: Financing, deals, listings, litigation, contested company responses and market-access changes for AI and chip firms with a US-China angle.
